User instruction: working with data in Column B, used formula =LEFT(B2,FIND(" ",B2)-1) to extract first name from string containing first name, surname, email. Need amended formula that correctly extracts both first name and surname, omitting email. Put this in Result should be column. Answer ranges Sheet1 C2:C3.

Context:
Sheet1:
A1 Name, B1 Employee, C1 Result Should Be
A2 formula =C8 cached 0 (weird)
B2 "Sharon Smith sharon.smith@BTRcom"
C2 value "Sharon Smith"
A3 formula =LEFT(B3,FIND(" ",B3)-1) cached Sam
B3 "Sam Landon sam@BTR.com"
C3 null

Need fill C2:C3 with formula? "Put this in the Result should be column." likely C2:C3. Need formula extracting first two words before email. Data B2 and B3. Need formula robust. Could use =LEFT(B2, FIND("@",B2)-1) then trim trailing space? For B2: "Sharon Smith sharon.smith@BTRcom" FIND @ gives position? Let's count: Sharon(6)+space=7, Smith(5)=12, space=13, sharon.smith(12?) Let's compute: "Sharon Smith sharon.smith@BTRcom". Characters: S1 h2 a3 r4 o5 n6 space7 S8 m9 i10 t11 h12 space13 s14 h15 a16 r17 o18 n19 .20 s21 m22 i23 t24 h25 @26. LEFT(B2, FIND("@",B2)-1) = first 25 chars = "Sharon Smith sharon.smith" includes email local part. Need omit email entirely. Need first name and surname only. Could use =LEFT(B2, FIND(" ",B2, FIND(" ",B2)+1)-1) i.e. up to second space. For B2: first space pos7, second space pos13, LEFT 12 = "Sharon Smith". For B3: "Sam Landon sam@BTR.com": first space pos4, second space pos11? Sam(3) space4 Landon(6) -> 10, space11, sam... second space pos11, LEFT 10 = "Sam Landon". Good. Formula: =LEFT(B2,FIND(" ",B2,FIND(" ",B2)+1)-1). Need fill C2:C3. Use fill_formula with top-left C2 formula referencing B2. It will translate to B3.

Need consider if email may have no space? But given format first name surname email. Could also use =TRIM(LEFT(B2,FIND("@",B2)-1)) but that leaves local part if no space? Actually if string "Sharon Smith sharon.smith@BTRcom", LEFT before @ includes "Sharon Smith sharon.smith", TRIM doesn't remove. Need second space.

Could use =LEFT(B2, FIND(" ",B2, FIND(" ",B2)+1)-1). This is classic. Need ensure formula string begins =. Use fill_formula range C2:C3.

Need output JSON object only. route operations, summary, operations. Ensure no markdown.

Check schema: operations array min 1. FillFormula properties op, sheet, range, formula. Good.

Need maybe C2 currently has value "Sharon Smith" but answer range includes C2. We can set formula. It will overwrite. Good.

Potential issue: A2 formula =C8 but C8 not in context? materialised=8 maybe C8? But not relevant. We preserve.

Need final JSON exactly.
